properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-04, after the "did we build this right?" census (docs/built-right-review.md, sourcing BL-198..BL-203): "this exercise of retrospective design choices I think should be a skill within reflow2. This exercise of the agent being able to see the design in the current state and say, 'you know what, we could have done this better' is a good thing... I'm not sure, but being retrospective in analyzing what you've done is probably a good thing." THE IDEA: a served skill that reads a design in its CURRENT state and reports where it would have been built differently — the counterpart to check-health (which asks how the design is SHAPED) and detect-and-ask (which asks what the design MEANS). HIS CANDIDATE QUESTION LIST, in his own words, four groups: STRUCTURE AND SETUP — did I use the right layout or pattern; is the setup easy to understand; can other people read and change this easily; did I keep things too joined together, or are they separate. SPEED AND EFFICIENCY — does this use too much time, space or power; where is the main slowdown or bottleneck; can I do tasks at the same time to speed things up; did I save data or results I do not need to keep. WEAK POINTS AND RISKS — what happens if a key part breaks right now; did I handle bad inputs or errors safely; where is the system likely to slow down or crash under heavy use; is private data or system access safe from outside threats. FUTURE CHANGES — how hard is it to add new features later; will this break if the size or user count grows ten times bigger; did I leave clear notes or guides for the next person. WHAT ARGUES FOR IT: the census that prompted this produced six backlog rows in one sitting, including BL-199, which explained why BL-176 had been invisible to self-host for eleven releases — so the exercise demonstrably finds things no existing instrument found. Several of his groups already have computations that exist and are not gathered anywhere: modularity and misplaced capabilities and god-components answer "too joined together"; granularity_report answers "did the build separate what the design distinguishes"; maturity_report's frontier answers "what did we leave until last"; ility_report already maps findings onto quality axes and reports NOT INFORMED where nothing computes. WHAT ARGUES AGAINST IT, recorded beside the idea rather than used to kill it: reflow2 has one hard-won rule against exactly this shape — BL-179, where Anthony himself objected that "avoid monoliths" is "kind of a subjective ask", and the resolution was that reflow2 does not detect monoliths, it detects that two records the design ALREADY HOLDS disagree, and RULES ON NEITHER SIDE. A skill that asks sixteen questions in prose and lets an agent answer them would reintroduce precisely the subjective grading that ruling removed. The strongest form of the idea is therefore the one where every question is backed by a computation over records the design already holds, and any question with no such computation says NOT INFORMED rather than inviting an opinion — which is ility_report's discipline applied to a skill. That is a separate open question and is recorded as dec:idea-retrospective-asks-or-computes. ALSO OPEN, NOT ASKED HERE: whether the reviewer should be the same agent that built the thing (the census was, and its blind spot was real — it took a mechanical three-way diff, not judgement, to find BL-199).
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 serve a retrospective design-review skill?
properties.rationale: Recorded so the idea is not lost while it is still an idea. Nothing here is intent: no Requirement, no Capability, and no claim that reflow2 will build this. The counter-argument is recorded beside the idea rather than used against it, per the brainstorm skill — an idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning.
